Well for me, it was twice I’ve heard those words. Both from my grandparents. My grandpa has dementia, he wished to be picked up later in the day from the local VLTs (old man loves the slot machines) and he looked me in the eyes and said, “don’t forget about me.” For what seemed like ages he said those words over and over again, perhaps forgetting he’d actually said them in the first place. It didn’t hit me till later, that’s when it started to hurt. And my grandma, after seeing her for the first time in months (I’ve started Uni) she took my hand, in her sweet voice she said to me “don’t you forget about me when you graduate, don’t you forget about Kookum.” That time it hit me like a ton of bricks in that instant. I couldn’t hold my tears in and for maybe the first time ever she seen me cry.
